body:
## What changed

Closes ticket 02 of the parity set (local, not committed). The draft's seven blockers are resolved.

**Host seam.** `HostExtensionServices.loadDependency(packageName)` resolves a module from Tau's own npm dependencies, the way `loadRuntimeExtension` already does for Pi extensions. A bundled kit's host half runs from a cache file under userData, from which `createRequire` cannot see the app's `node_modules`, and node-pty finds its `spawn-helper` beside its own binary only where npm put it, so bundling is not an option either. No permission (an in-process package could reach the module anyway); denied in a worker like every live object. Extension API 1.7.0; `@tau/kits` requires `^1.7.0`. Documented in `docs/EXTENSIONS.md` and the README's worker table.

**Terminal Kit** (`kits/terminal/`, host + desktop, in-process):
- pty sessions filed under the workspace the host has open; a thread's own worktree is where its shell starts when that thread is open. Capacity (8 per workspace) counts by that root.
- terminals die with the workspace: `beforeWorkspace` names the root the host moves to, every shell of another root is closed then. They survive a client reload (replay by byte offset, no double drawing) and a thread's runtime closing.
- an exited shell stays listed with its exit code until the user closes or restarts it; `restart` puts a fresh shell in the same place under a new id. Killing a running shell and dropping an ended one are the same command.
- the panel groups terminals by the thread on screen and marks the ones running in another thread ("another thread", plus a status line) instead of killing them. xterm takes its colors from the workbench tokens and is rebuilt only when the session changes, not on every resize.
- Windows keeps `ComSpec` instead of falling back to `/bin/sh`.
- xterm moves to devDependencies: it is bundled into the kit's desktop half; only node-pty ships.
- registered in `kits/kit-lifecycle.test.tsx` and the `docs/CORE.md` kit and stylesheet tables.

**Not a stage tab.** The ticket prefers a stage document; the stage's tab kinds are core-owned (`src/workbench/stage.ts`) and there is no contribution seam for an interactive document, so the kit uses the dock panel the ticket also allows. A stage seam would be a separate core change.

## Verification

- `npm run lint`: pass (11 pre-existing warnings)
- `npm run typecheck`: pass
- `npm test`: 315 files, 2201 tests pass
- `npm run build`: pass; `dist-kits/tau.terminal/host.cjs` references node-pty only through `loadDependency`
- node-pty's darwin-arm64 prebuild spawns a real shell under plain Node
- Isolated instance (`npm run dev:instance --fresh`, driven over CDP): a real zsh prints what was typed; `exit 5` shows "shell exited with 5" and Restart opens a fresh prompt; a renderer reload replays the scrollback; opening a new thread marks the first thread's terminal as "another thread" with the status note. Instance stopped afterwards, nothing touched the real Tau data.

## Not verified here

- Web client in a browser (the panel declares the `web` profile and the lifecycle test activates it there; the host-event path is the same transport).
- Packaged installer, Linux and Windows.
